sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: create_marker
tools.description: Create a marker object from a marker string expression. marker: The string representation of a marker expression, e.g. 'python_version >= "3.6"' -> "<Marker('python_version >= "3.6"')>".

tools.name: evaluate_marker
tools.description:
Evaluate a marker against an environment to determine if it matches.
    
    Args:
        marker: A marker string to evaluate
        environment: Mapping containing keys and values to override the detected environment
        context: The context in which the marker is evaluated, which influences what marker names are considered valid.
                 Accepted values are "metadata" (for core metadata; default), "lock_file", and "requirement".
    
    Returns:
        True if the marker matches the environment, otherwise False
    
    Example:
        >>> evaluate_marker('python_version >= "3.6"', {"python_version": "3.8"})
        True

tools.name: parse_metadata_from_email
tools.description:
Parse metadata from email headers.
    
    Args:
        data: Email headers containing distribution metadata
        validate: Whether to validate the parsed metadata
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary containing the parsed metadata fields
        
    Example:
        >>> parse_metadata_from_email('Name: mypackage\nVersion: 1.0\n', True)
        {'name': 'mypackage', 'version': '1.0'}

tools.name: create_full_version_range
tools.description: Return the full version range that includes all PEP 440 versions. admit_arbitrary: whether to admit arbitrary strings as valid versions; prereleases: whether to include pre-release versions. Example: create_full_version_range() -> "<VersionRange object>"

tools.name: create_empty_version_range
tools.description: Return an empty version range that includes no versions. prereleases: whether pre-release versions should be considered in the version range -> {}.

tools.name: create_singleton_version_range
tools.description: Return a version range that contains only a single specific version. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> '{1.0}'. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: check_version_in_range
tools.description:
Check if a version is contained within a version range.
    
    :param specifier_set: A specifier set that can be converted to a version range (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0')
    :param version: The version to check against the range
    :return: True if the version is contained in the range, False otherwise
    
    >>> check_version_in_range('>=1.0,<2.0', '1.5')
    True
    >>> check_version_in_range('>=1.0,<2.0', '2.0')
    False

tools.name: intersect_version_ranges
tools.description: Get the intersection of two version ranges. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier. Example: intersect_version_ranges('>=1.0', '<2.0') -> '>=1.0,<2.0'.

tools.name: union_version_ranges
tools.description:
Get the union of two version ranges. version_range_a: First version range in PEP 440 format, version_range_b: Second version range in PEP 440 format.
    
    >>> union_version_ranges(">=1.0", "<2.0")
    '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: complement_version_range
tools.description: Get the complement of a version range. version_range: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet, e.g. '>=1.0' -> '<1.0'.

tools.name: create_specifier
tools.description: Create a version specifier from a string. spec: A version specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0.0' -> '<=2.0.0'. prereleases: Whether to include pre-releases.

tools.name: create_specifier_set
tools.description: Create a set of version specifiers from a string or iterable. specifiers: A string representation of a specifier or a comma-separated list of specifiers, e.g. '>=3.0,!=3.1' -> SpecifierSet object serialized as string. prereleases: Whether to accept prerelease versions if applicable.

tools.name: check_version_in_specifier_set
tools.description:
Check if a version is contained within a specifier set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set: A string representing the version specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1')
        version: The version string to check against the specifier set
        prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440.
        installed: Whether or not the item is installed. If set to True, it will accept prerelease versions even if the specifier does not allow them.
        
    Returns:
        True if the version is contained in the specifier set, False otherwise.
        
    Example:
        >>> check_version_in_specifier_set('>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1', '1.2.3')
        True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
tools.description: Check whether a specifier set can never be satisfied. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=2.0,<1.0' -> True.

tools.name: convert_specifier_set_to_range
tools.description: Convert a specifier set to a version range. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'.

tools.name: check_specifier_set_subset
tools.description: Check if one specifier set is a subset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check against. >>> check_specifier_set_subset('>=3.12,<3.13', '>=3.12') True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_superset
tools.description: Check if one specifier set is a superset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check against. >>> check_specifier_set_superset('>=3.12', '>=3.12,<3.13') True

tools.name: check_specifier_sets_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two specifier sets share no matching versions.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set1 (str): First specifier set string
        specifier_set2 (str): Second specifier set string
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the sets share no matching versions, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_sets_disjoint("<3.12", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: check_version_in_specifier
tools.description: Check if a version is contained within a specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=1.2.3'. version: The version string to check against the specifier. prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this Specifier. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440. >>> check_version_in_specifier('>=1.2.3', '1.2.3') True

tools.name: create_tag
tools.description: Create a tag object from interpreter, ABI, and platform strings. interpreter: The interpreter name, e.g. 'py'. abi: The ABI that a wheel supports, e.g. 'cp37m'. platform: The OS/platform the wheel supports, e.g. 'win_amd64'. Example: create_tag('py', 'cp37m', 'win_amd64') -> 'py-cp37m-win_amd64'.

tools.name: parse_tag_string
tools.description: Parse a tag string into a frozenset of Tag instances. tag: The tag to parse, e.g. "py3-none-any". validate_order: Check whether compressed tag set components are in sorted order. limit: The maximum number of tags to parse. -> frozenset of tag strings

tools.name: generate_cpython_tags
tools.description: Generate CPython interpreter tags for wheel compatibility. python_version: target Python version as [major, minor], e.g. [3, 9]. abis: compatible ABIs, e.g. ['cp39', 'abi3']. platforms: compatible platforms, e.g. ['linux_x86_64']. Returns list of tag strings like 'cp39-cp39-linux_x86_64'.

tools.name: generate_generic_tags
tools.description: Generate generic interpreter tags. interpreter: The name of the interpreter, e.g. 'cp39'. abis: Iterable of compatible ABIs, e.g. ['cp39', 'abi3']. platforms: Iterable of compatible platforms, e.g. ['linux_x86_64']. -> List of tag strings like 'cp39-none-linux_x86_64'.

tools.name: generate_compatible_tags
tools.description: Generate tags for interpreters compatible with a specified Python version. python_version: A one- or two-item sequence representing the compatible version of Python, e.g. [3, 8]. interpreter: The name of the interpreter (if known), e.g. 'cp38'. Example: generate_compatible_tags([3, 9], 'cp39') -> ['cp39-none-any', 'py39-none-linux_x86_64', 'py38-none-linux_x86_64', 'py37-none-linux_x86_64', 'py36-none-linux_x86_64', 'py35-none-linux_x86_64', 'py34-none-linux_x86_64', 'py33-none-linux_x86_64', 'py32-none-linux_x86_64', 'py31-none-linux_x86_64', 'py30-none-linux_x86_64', 'py39-none-any']

tools.name: generate_system_tags
tools.description: Generate the sequence of tag triples supported by the running interpreter. warn: Whether warnings should be logged -> ["cp39-cp39-linux_x86_64", ...]

tools.name: canonicalize_package_name
tools.description: Normalize a package name to its canonical form. name: The package name to normalize. validate: Check whether the name is a valid distribution name. >>> canonicalize_package_name("Django") 'django'

tools.name: canonicalize_version_string
tools.description: Return a canonical form of a version string. version: A version string to canonicalize, e.g. '1.0.0' -> '1'. strip_trailing_zero: Whether to strip trailing zeros from the release segment, e.g. '1.0.0' with strip_trailing_zero=False -> '1.0.0'.

tools.name: parse_wheel_filename
tools.description: Parse a wheel filename into its components. filename: The name of the wheel file, e.g. 'foo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl' -> {'name': 'foo', 'version': '1.0', 'build': [], 'tags': ['py3-none-any']}. validate_order: Check whether compressed tag set components are in sorted order.

tools.name: parse_sdist_filename
tools.description: Parse an sdist filename into its components. filename: The name of the sdist file, e.g. 'foo-1.0.tar.gz' -> {"name": "foo", "version": "1.0"}.

tools.name: create_version
tools.description: Create a version object from a version string. version_string: A string representation of a version conforming to PEP 440, e.g. '1.0a5' -> '<Version('1.0a5')>'.

tools.name: parse_version_string
tools.description:
Parse the given version string.
    
    This is identical to the Version constructor.
    
    >>> parse_version_string('1.0.dev1')
    '1.0.dev1'
    
    :param version: The version string to parse.
    :raises ValueError: When the version string is not a valid version.

tools.name: get_public_version
tools.description: Get the public portion of a version. version: A version string to extract the public portion from e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: get_base_version
tools.description: Get the base version of a version. version: A version string to extract the base version from e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: check_is_prerelease
tools.description: Check if a version is a pre-release. version: A version string to check if it is a pre-release -> true if pre-release, false otherwise.

tools.name: check_is_postrelease
tools.description: Check if a version is a post-release. version: A version string to check if it is a post-release -> true if post-release, false otherwise.

tools.name: check_is_devrelease
tools.description: Check if a version is a development release. version: A version string to check if it's a development release -> true if development release, false otherwise.

tools.name: get_major_version
tools.description: Get the major version component. version: A version string to parse and extract the major version from -> 1.

tools.name: get_minor_version
tools.description: Get the minor version component. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3' -> 2.

tools.name: get_micro_version
tools.description: Get the micro version component. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3' -> 3.
